context: First live attempt at the #50 D7 gate (unattended nine-step minimum-viable-demo run) since #154 closed all 7 remaining mission-lifecycle HTTP router stubs (PR #160, PR #161, merged 2026-08-17). Run against origin/main @ 2dc1c72 on a dedicated local branch (gate-50-live-run) created from origin/main so as not to disturb other agents' in-progress branches found mid-merge-conflict in this working tree at session start.
verdict_reason: The mission-lifecycle HTTP API (all 11 routers, now genuinely wired per #154) supports create -> authorize -> snapshot -> preflight -> start, which moves a mission to SNAPSHOTTED -> VALIDATING. Nothing in the reachable HTTP surface, and nothing running automatically in the background, ever calls orchestrator.transitions.transition() again after that point. A mission started through the real API is empirically confirmed stuck at VALIDATING indefinitely (60s unattended observation, zero state change) even though contracts.state_machine.TRANSITIONS legally permits VALIDATING -> BASELINE and the real baseline/fuzzing/patch/verification code (workers/baseline/run.py, workers/fuzzing/, orchestrator/candidates.py, orchestrator/verification.py) exists and is unit-tested. Nothing wires the state machine's automatic stages to that code. The nine-step demo (CEO doc §3) cannot be driven end to end through the real HTTP API today. Not an environment problem, not a #154 regression — #154's own acceptance criteria stopped at 'start' and never claimed more.

new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.title: SNAPSHOT_SOURCE_ROOT (/demo/repositories) was never mounted into control-api in any compose profile, dev or finale
new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.scope: devops / infrastructure compose config — fixed in this session
new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.detail: config.settings.base.SNAPSHOT_SOURCE_ROOT defaults to BASE_DIR.parent.parent/demo/repositories. Neither docker-compose.yml (dev) nor docker-compose.finale.yml mounted the repo's demo/repositories/ directory into the control-api container at that path. source="git" snapshot ingestion — the only way to hand the container a local demo target like pktcfg without a real git remote — had therefore never actually worked containerized in any profile. Confirmed by exec into the container: /demo/repositories did not exist.
new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.fix: Added a read-only bind mount ../../demo/repositories:/demo/repositories:ro to the control-api service (and, for parity, the worker service) in both infrastructure/compose/docker-compose.finale.yml and infrastructure/compose/docker-compose.yml.
new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.verified: docker exec into the rebuilt container confirmed /demo/repositories/pktcfg is now visible and readable with the expected file listing.

new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.title: ARTIFACT_ROOT (snapshot content-addressed store) pointed inside the finale image's read-only /app, and the fallback fix (a named volume) was still root-owned against a non-root, capability-dropped container
new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.scope: devops / infrastructure compose + Dockerfile — fixed in this session
new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.detail: Two-stage discovery. (1) config.settings.base.ARTIFACT_ROOT defaults to BASE_DIR/var/artifacts, i.e. /app/var/artifacts — inside the finale runtime image's baked-in source tree, which is read_only: true at the container level. POST .../snapshot 500'd with OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system: '/app/var' the moment it tried to materialize the tar it had just built. (2) Repointing ARTIFACT_ROOT at a named volume (/var/lib/brahmadatta/artifacts) fixed the read-only problem but hit a second one: Docker creates named volumes empty and root-owned; the finale control-api container runs as uid 10001 (app) with cap_drop: ["ALL"] and no CHOWN capability, so it could not write into its own volume either — PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied. The pre-existing 'evidence' volume (for exported evidence bundles) has the identical latent bug; it had simply never been exercised by any prior partial verification, since nothing had reached mission teardown/export before #154 wired the routers that let a mission progress that far.
new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.fix: Set ARTIFACT_ROOT=/var/lib/brahmadatta/artifacts as an explicit env var on control-api (and worker) in docker-compose.finale.yml, added a new artifacts: named volume, and — to fix the ownership problem for both this new volume and the pre-existing evidence volume in one place — added `RUN mkdir -p /var/lib/brahmadatta/{artifacts,evidence} && chown -R app:app /var/lib/brahmadatta` to the runtime stage of infrastructure/compose/images/control-api.Dockerfile, before USER app:app. This relies on documented Docker behavior: a fresh named volume is seeded from whatever already exists at its mount point in the image, ownership included, on first mount.
new_bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session.verified: Rebuilt --no-cache, removed the already-initialized (root-owned) artifacts and evidence volumes, recreated the container, and confirmed via docker exec ls -la /var/lib/brahmadatta/ that both directories are now owned by app:app. Snapshot ingestion (step 3 below) then succeeded.

unresolved_blocker_reported_not_fixed.title: No mechanism — HTTP endpoint or automatic background process — advances a mission past VALIDATING
unresolved_blocker_reported_not_fixed.scope_note: This is application/orchestration engineering, not infrastructure. Per instructions, reported rather than attempted: this is the same size and shape of work as #154 itself (a full backend-developer + engineering-manager + cybersecurity + qa-engineer review cycle), not a small, clearly-scoped devops fix.
static_evidence: apps/control-api/api/routers/missions.py contains exactly 11 endpoints: create, list, get, authorize, snapshot, preflight, start, pause, cancel, events, events/replay. None of them, and nothing in evidence.py or system.py, ever calls contracts.state_machine target BASELINE/TRIAGE/STRESS_TEST/CORRELATE/PATCH/VERIFY/EXPORTING.

orchestrator/transitions.py's transition() is the sole writer of Mission.state. Its only two automatic (transaction.on_commit) side effects are teardown (on CANCELLING/terminal) and starting the model host lease (on entering PATCH) — neither of those advances the state machine itself.
start_mission() (missions/service.py:338) is documented as 'Start the autonomous workflow' but its implementation performs exactly one transition, SNAPSHOTTED -> VALIDATING, and returns.

workers/baseline/run.py's own module docstring states plainly: 'No orchestrator or event bus exists yet (#12), so nothing here posts these anywhere; emit_baseline_events is what a caller — the future orchestrator, or a script proving the D3 gate by hand — calls'. That caller was never built. Confirmed by grep: nothing under apps/control-api imports workers.baseline, workers.fuzzing, or workers.replay.
No Django signal (post_save/pre_save) exists anywhere in apps/control-api on the Mission model.

No django_rq / celery / rq dependency exists in apps/control-api/requirements.txt or config/settings. The finale compose file's worker service (profile "worker", not activated by default) runs `python manage.py rqworker default` as its default command — a command that would itself fail immediately since django-rq is not installed; this service has never been exercised end to end.
No apps/control-api/*/management/commands/*.py exists at all (find returned empty) — there is no CLI driver either.
unresolved_blocker_reported_not_fixed.empirical_evidence: See transcript below. A mission driven for real through create -> authorize -> snapshot -> preflight -> start reached VALIDATING at 2026-08-17T05:21:29.029Z and was polled every 10s for 60s unattended; state, progress, and last_event_sequence never changed. allowed_transitions in the mission detail response correctly listed BASELINE as a legal next state per the state machine — confirming the block is 'nothing calls it', not 'the state machine forbids it'. The same gap recurs one step further out: cancel_mission (VALIDATING -> CANCELLING) worked and correctly triggered teardown (real, wired, confirmed via the TEARDOWN_CONFIRMED event), but CANCELLING -> CANCELLED has the identical problem — orchestrator/teardown.py's teardown_started_compute() only reaps compute and emits events, it never calls transition() to finalize the mission — so the test mission is permanently stuck in CANCELLING too, not CANCELLED.
unresolved_blocker_reported_not_fixed.recommendation: This needs a scoped ticket the same shape as #154: a mission-stage driver that, for each state VALIDATING through EXPORTING (and CANCELLING -> CANCELLED / FAILED -> FAILED-confirmed), actually invokes the already-built, already-tested stage code (workers/baseline, workers/fuzzing, orchestrator/candidates.py, orchestrator/verification.py, teardown.py's own missing final transition) and then calls orchestrator.transitions.transition() to record the outcome. Whether that driver is synchronous-in-request, a background poller, or a real RQ/Celery worker (the compose scaffolding for the latter already exists but is unwired and untested) is an architecture decision for the CTO/software-architect, not a call this report makes.
